result.title: A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering
result.summary: Bias in transformer-based models is a growing concern as these architectures become more prevalent in automated decision-making systems, such as prediction models for hiring, lending, and clinical treatment recommendation. Mechanistic interpretability (MI) is a growing body of work that measures meaningful causal effects of activations on model output by identifying human-interpretable features encoded in model activations. When such features correspond to sensitive attributes, they provide a direct way to quantify the bias those attributes introduce and to causally intervene to mitigate it. However, counterfactual fairness (CF) methods have not been systematically adapted to this setting of intervening on interpretable mechanisms in transformers. We propose a framework, Mechanistic Interpretability for Counterfactual Fairness (MICF), that utilizes MI tools to reformulate CF constraints in terms of transformer activations, unifying former approaches into a single pipeline for fairness analysis in transformers. MICF does not require a prior causal model or specific transformer architecture. We evaluate MICF on real-world tabular data and show that CF can be improved across different prediction tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MICF 框架，用机制可解释性工具把反事实公平约束改写为 transformer 激活层面的条件，在无需预设因果模型或特定架构的前提下统一既有做法，并在真实表格数据上验证公平性可改善。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「定位激活中可解释特征并做激活转向与因果干预」的流程，可供核查是否能用于编辑或检验 VLM 内部承载视觉证据与推理状态的表示；但论文限于表格预测的公平性，未涉及多模态推理，迁移仅为可能线索。
